notes: ACCESS: plain direct HTTP fetch worked throughout, no block. Checked main nav (no 'New'/'New Arrivals'/'What's New' item exists in the mega-menu), footer, homepage announcement bar, a department page (all-lighting - no 'new' links found there either), and the collections sitemap grepped for new/arrival/just-in/latest/recently-added keywords - found ~15 'new-*' collections. Only /collections/new qualifies as a candidate row: real PLP (grid, facets, sort, theme product-count element), heading literally 'New', qty=38, and its live/current status was verified by sampling 24 product slugs from its first grid page against sitemap_products_1.xml - 24/24 present in the current live catalogue. Flagged for manual review rather than accepted outright because it is NOT linked from any current site navigation, footer, homepage promotion, or department landing page (only discoverable via the collections sitemap/direct URL), and its on-page description is generic reused brand boilerplate rather than New-Arrivals-specific copy. EXCLUDED as unlinked, internally-inconsistent department/style facets (same non-exposure concern as above, and their counts do NOT cleanly partition the 'New' parent - e.g. new-bedding=29 exceeds new-bed-bath=22, its supposed parent department, proving these are not a coherent taxonomy but stale/independent legacy collections): new-lighting(8), new-furniture(4), new-home-decor(2), new-bed-bath(22), new-hardware(3), new-bedding(29), new-rugs(3), new-kitchen-dining(1), new-utility(3), new-modern(3), new-modern-favorites(15). EXCLUDED new-2021(0 products, dated/stale) and newbury-collection(0 products; 'Newbury' is a named product line, not a New-Arrivals concept) - both zero-product anyway. EXCLUDED new-trade-discount-collection(98): a B2B/trade-program pricing collection ('new' refers to the trade program launch, not product recency), unrelated to New Arrivals merchandising.
